name: Legumes & Pulses
tagline: Beans, lentils, chickpeas, and heritage varieties from smallholder farms worldwide. Among the most nutritious and land-efficient foods on the planet.

learn.how_we_evaluate: In this category, origin transparency and farming method are the primary signals. Legumes are among the most sustainably grown foods on the planet — they fix nitrogen and require little irrigation — but that story is often missing from the label. We look for named growing region, named variety, and honest organic or fair trade claims.
what_to_look_for: Named country and region of origin
Named variety where relevant (Puy lentils, Castelluccio lentils, Borlotti, etc.)
Fair trade or direct trade relationship disclosed for imported pulses
Harvest year or crop year on packaging
red_flags: No country of origin — especially for canned legumes
Generic variety names only — 'green lentils' with no origin
Long ingredient lists in canned products — legumes need only legumes, water, salt

key_terms.definition: Some European legumes carry geographic protection — Puy lentils (AOP), Castelluccio lentils (IGP), Fagiolina del Trasimeno. These protect variety, origin, and traditional growing methods.
Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen through root bacteria, reducing the need for synthetic fertilisers. This makes them one of the most land-efficient and climate-friendly protein sources available.
